samples.summary: Archive-drop on revocation keys on HTTP 403 only, but workspace/document deletion answers 404 — so a full local copy of a team document survives loss of authority and is then republished into the ex-member's own workspace
samples.evidence:
`isRevoked` (offline-runtime.tsx:103-110) returns true only for `HttpError` status 403, and `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (lib/offline-erase.ts:541-549) drops an archive on that answer and nothing else.

But the 403 only arises while the *document row still exists*: `GET documents/:id` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:169-177) does `documentService.document({id})` first and throws `NotFoundException` (404) at line 171 before `assertMember` can throw `ForbiddenException` (workspace.service.ts:241). And `Document.workspace` is `onDelete: Cascade` (packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma:91), so deleting a workspace deletes its documents.

Chain: owner deletes a shared workspace (or removes a member and then deletes the document). The ex-member's device still holds an archive — a full compressed snapshot plus change log of that document. Next session: `fetchDocuments()` no longer lists it → `isRevoked(id)` sees 404 → returns false → archive kept. `offerRecoverableWork` (offline-runtime.tsx, the `catch` that `continue`s only when status !== 404) then proceeds with `workspaceId === undefined` → `resolveRecoveryDestination(undefined)` (lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts:204-239) falls back to a workspace the user is sole member of → `createWorkspaceDocument` materialises the whole document in a workspace the ex-member owns.

This is exactly the harm `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` pass `dropArchives: true` to prevent on the *requesting* device (api/workspaces.ts:136,167) — and the member's own device is the one place the design says the reconcile is the only backstop (api/workspaces.ts:148-153). The 403 discriminator cannot see the cascade case at all.

samples.summary: `offlineInPlay` gate can leave stored document content with no sweep, no revocation reconcile and no logout erase — the three backstops the design names for a shared device
samples.evidence:
`OfflineRuntime` is the sole production caller of `rememberOfflineUser`, `retryPendingOfflineErase` and `store.collectStale()` (grep over packages/frontend/src: offline-runtime.tsx:66, :134, :146 and nothing else). It is mounted only when `supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(me.id)` (PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30, :58).

After a pin rollback below `MinClientKeyVersion` (which the comment at PrivateRoute.tsx:50-53 explicitly anticipates), `supportsClientKey()` is false, so the gate reduces to the *current* account's preference. Two reachable states then have content on disk with the gate closed:

1. Account B signs in on a device where account A stored documents under a capable build. B never opted in → gate false → runtime never mounts → A's entries get no 30-day sweep and no reconcile. The design names that sweep as the backstop for exactly the account that never returns.
2. Account A turned the preference off and the erase threw. `watchForOfflineDisable` (lib/offline-erase.ts:620-622) only logs — unlike `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, it records no pending erase. A's preference is now off, so on a sub-floor build the gate is false and nothing ever collects the residue.

Secondary consequence: with the runtime unmounted, `rememberOfflineUser` never runs, so `offlineUserId()` (lib/offline-erase.ts:98-107) falls back to a stale `wafflebase-offline-user` in localStorage. A logout by the *current* user then drives `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` against the previous account's id (lib/offline-erase.ts:311-332), erasing the wrong account's store while leaving the signer-out's own untouched.

samples.summary: `Math.random()` fallback mints the client-key salt, which is the only thing making the Yorkie client key unguessable
samples.evidence:
`randomSecret()` (durable-session.ts:244-257) falls back to `Math.floor(Math.random() * 256)` when `crypto.getRandomValues` is absent. That value is the `deviceSecret` salt in `wb:{deviceSecret}:{userId}:{docKey}` (durable-session.ts:106-108), and the file's own doc comment (lines 80-90) states the salt is what stops a workspace peer — who already knows `userId` and `docKey` — from deriving the key and calling `DeactivateClient`, since Yorkie authorises those on token validity alone.

`Math.random()` is not a CSPRNG and its state is recoverable from a handful of outputs, so a fallback-minted salt is derivable by the very attacker the salt exists to stop. The inline justification ("`navigator.locks` and `crypto` are both secure-context APIs") is half wrong — `crypto.getRandomValues` is available in insecure contexts; only `crypto.subtle` is gated. The path does appear unreachable in practice because `supportsDurableSession()` requires `navigator.locks`, which is secure-context-only, so `durableClientKey` is never called where `crypto` would be missing. Throwing (fail closed) would match the module's stated posture better than a weak secret.

samples.summary: A session that expires rather than being signed out leaves full document content in IndexedDB on a shared device for up to 30 days
samples.evidence:
`logout({ eraseLocalData: 'none' })` from the 401 arm (api/auth.ts:256-277) makes the `eraseLocalData !== "none" && res?.ok` guard at api/auth.ts:134 skip `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` entirely. The stated design promise is that "signing out is where it must stop outliving the session — the whole point of the setting being per device is that the device may be shared" (api/auth.ts:116-119).

On a kiosk or shared workstation the commonest way a session ends is the cookie expiring while the user walks away, not a deliberate Log out — and on that path nothing is erased. The residue is only reclaimed by the 30-day sweep, and that sweep runs from `OfflineRuntime`, which for the *next* user of the machine is gated on their own preference (see the PrivateRoute finding). The trade-off (don't destroy the un-pushed change log on an event the user did not choose) is reasoned and defensible; what is missing is any bound tighter than 30 days on the shared-device exposure it creates — e.g. erasing live entries while keeping archives, which `dropAllForUser` already supports via `keepArchives`.

samples.summary: `lastKnown` keeps a durable client mounted under a signed-out identity, so a window exists where a newly signed-in account's edits are written into the previous account's store scope
samples.evidence:
`const person = me ?? lastKnown.current` (collab-document-provider.tsx:214-218) deliberately ignores a `null` from `fetchMeOptional`, keeping the `DurableYorkieProvider` mounted with the previous user's `clientKey` and `userId` (lines 383-391). `fetchMeOptional` does not go through `fetchWithAuth`, so it does not redirect — the tab survives.

On a shared device, if user A's session ends and user B signs in from another tab, this tab keeps writing through A's client key and A's store scope (the store's `isPersistenceEnabled` asks `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(A) && isOfflineWritePermitted(A)`, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx) while `authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken}` now returns B's token. Edits made between B's sign-in and this tab's focus refetch of `['me','optional']` land under A's scope. The window is short and requires tab switching on a shared machine, and `denyOfflineWrites` closes it when A signed out deliberately — but not when A's session merely expired, which is the same path the `lastKnown` ref exists to survive.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed chain is present and reachable as described. `isRevoked` (offline-runtime.tsx:103-110) returns true only for HttpError status 403, and that boolean is the sole trigger for `archives: "drop"` in `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:541-549). The backend's `GET documents/:id` throws NotFoundException at document.controller.ts:171 *before* `assertMember` can throw Forbidden at :173, so once the row is gone the 403 signal is unobtainable; `Document.workspace` is `onDelete: Cascade` (prisma/schema.prisma:126 — the finding's :91 citation points at a different model, but the Document cascade is real), so deleting a workspace deletes its documents. On the ex-member's next session the document is absent from `fetchDocuments()` and answers 404, so the archive is kept; `offerRecoverableWork` then `continue`s only for non-404 errors (offline-runtime.tsx:296-301), leaving `workspaceId === undefined`, and `resolveRecoveryDestination(undefined)` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:204-239) falls back to a sole-member or first workspace, after which `recoverOfflineCopy` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:284-307) calls `createWorkspaceDocument` + `applyImportedContent`, publishing the rehydrated snapshot into a workspace the ex-member owns. No out-of-diff guard closes the hole: `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` pass `dropArchives: true` only on the requesting device (api/workspaces.ts:136,167) and the code's own comment (api/workspaces.ts:148-153) states the removed member's device is reached by nothing else and relies entirely on this reconcile. `collectStale()` only bounds the window at thirty days. This is content outliving the authority to read it plus a republication path, which is in the access-control / sensitive-data lane rather than the correctness lens, and it matches the repository's own stated rule at api/workspaces.ts:120-124. The deliberate design comment at offline-runtime.tsx:89-102 explains the trade-off but does not eliminate the gap, so no refutation ground applies.

1. Account B signs in on a device where account A stored documents under a capable build. B never opted in → gate false → runtime never mounts → A's entries get no 30-day sweep and no reconcile. The design names that sweep as the backstop for exactly the account that never returns.
2. Account A turned the preference off and the erase threw. `watchForOfflineDisable` (lib/offline-erase.ts:620-622) only logs — unlike `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, it records no pending erase. A's preference is now off, so on a sub-floor build the gate is false and nothing ever collects the residue.

Secondary consequence: with the runtime unmounted, `rememberOfflineUser` never runs, so `offlineUserId()` (lib/offline-erase.ts:98-107) falls back to a stale `wafflebase-offline-user` in localStorage. A logout by the *current* user then drives `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` against the previous account's id (lib/offline-erase.ts:311-332), erasing the wrong account's store while leaving the signer-out's own untouched.

verdict.reason: Every cited fact checks out in the tree. PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30/:58 is the only production mount of OfflineRuntime, and OfflineRuntime is the sole production caller of rememberOfflineUser (offline-runtime.tsx:66), retryPendingOfflineErase (:134) and store.collectStale() (:146). supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82, floor 0.7.23 at :24) is false in this tree today because package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22, so the gate reduces to the current account's per-account preference (offline-persistence-preference.ts:103-110). A device holding entries written under a capable build therefore gets no 30-day sweep, no revocation reconcile and no owed-erase retry whenever the signed-in account is not the consenting one — and the per-device answer that would cover it, hasOfflinePersistenceConsent() (offline-persistence-preference.ts:123-125, used at collab-document-provider.tsx:241), is not consulted. Scenario 2 is also accurate: watchForOfflineDisable only console.warns on a failed erase (offline-erase.ts:620-622) while eraseOfflineDataOnLogout records a pending erase (:339-343), so that residue has no retry queued. The secondary consequence is real and even broader than claimed: logout calls eraseOfflineDataOnLogout unconditionally (api/auth.ts:135), which resolves the victim through offlineUserId()'s stale localStorage mirror when the runtime never mounted (offline-erase.ts:311, :98-107), and App.tsx:118-138 shows signed-out-able routes outside PrivateRoute, so the wrong account's store can be erased while the signer-out's is left. No guard elsewhere makes any of this unreachable; this is sensitive-data retention/destruction on a shared device, squarely in the security lane.

finding.summary: `remove()` writes a full document archive to disk without consulting `isPersistenceEnabled` / `isOfflineWritePermitted`, so content can be re-materialized after the user revoked consent
finding.evidence:
`refuseIfDisabled()` is called on exactly three write paths — `saveSnapshot` (line 619), `appendChange` (661) and `saveMeta` (708). `remove()` (795-854) is a fourth write path: at line 840 it `put`s an `ArchiveRecord` carrying `record.snapshot`, `header?.meta` and the whole compressed change log into the `archives` object store, and it consults neither `this.isPersistenceEnabled` nor the erase denial.

Vector: the user switches the Settings toggle off. `watchForOfflineDisable` (offline-erase.ts:581) fires with `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` already false and starts `eraseOfflineData` → `dropAllForUser`, which purges headers/snapshots and only then calls `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, …)`. By design the durable client is deliberately left mounted across the toggle (collab-document-provider.tsx:232-255). If the SDK emits `LocalChangesDropped` and calls `remove(docKey)` during that window — or after the archive-drop half has already run — line 840 writes the full document snapshot back into `archives`. Nothing re-runs the erase, so that content sits on the disk the user just asked to be cleared until the thirty-day sweep. The same window exists on the logout path: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` calls `denyOfflineWrites(who)` first (offline-erase.ts:330) specifically so live writes are refused for the duration of the erase, and `remove()` is the one write that ignores that denial.

The other three writers were given the guard for exactly this reason; `remove()` was missed. A `refuseIfDisabled(docKey)` (or an `isOfflineWritePermitted` check) before the `put` at 840 closes it — deleting without archiving is the correct behaviour once the user has asked for the content to be gone.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `remove()` writes the archive `put` without consulting `isPersistenceEnabled` or the erase denial. The code does the opposite. At wafflebase-doc-store.ts:819-821 the archive decision is computed as `const losing = this.expectedLosses.has(documentKey) && this.isPersistenceEnabled?.() !== false;` and the `ArchiveRecord` `put` at line 852 is guarded by `if (record && losing)` at line 841 — so a store whose persistence predicate returns false deletes the entry and archives nothing. The erase-denial half is covered by the same predicate: durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:185-187 wires `isPersistenceEnabled` as `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(userId) && isOfflineWritePermitted(userId)`, so both the Settings-toggle path and the logout `denyOfflineWrites` path (offline-erase.ts:186,208,330) drive `losing` to false. The doc comment at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:795-803 states this intent verbatim, including why `remove()` refuses silently rather than throwing. A regression test at wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:872-897 exercises the exact vector claimed (seed, flip enabled=false, expectLoss, remove) and asserts the archive list is empty. The reviewer's cited line numbers (put at 840, method 795-854) do not match the working tree (put at 852, method 805-866), and docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-lessons.md:189-195 describes this as an already-fixed historical defect — suggesting the finding was drawn from that write-up rather than from current source. The described ungated code is not present.

finding.summary: The offline opt-in is keyed per *device* only, so one account's consent causes a different account's document content to be written to that machine's disk without that user ever being asked
finding.evidence:
`STORAGE_KEY = "wafflebase-offline-persistence"` is a single, unqualified `localStorage` key — there is no user component. `CollabDocumentProvider` reads it through `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` and combines it only with `supportsClientKey()`, `permitted` and the signed-in identity (collab-document-provider.tsx:217-229); nothing checks *who* turned it on.

Vector, on the shared machine this feature's threat model is built around: user A signs in, enables "Save documents on this device", and signs out (or their session simply expires). The preference survives — it is device-local by design. User B then signs in on the same browser profile; `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` returns true for them, `useDurableDocument` elects their tab, and every document B opens is written to that disk under B's own store scope. B was never shown the toggle, never agreed to it, and the Settings switch will read as already-on if they ever look.

The design doc reasons carefully about the opposite direction only — `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § Turning it on argues an account-level setting "would follow the user onto a shared machine and re-enable there" — and does not address that a device-level setting applies to every subsequent user of that device. B's exposure is bounded by B's own deliberate sign-out, but the consent that caused it was A's. Scoping the preference key by user id (`wafflebase-offline-persistence:{userId}`) preserves the per-device property the design wants while making the consent the actual user's.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that the offline opt-in is a single unqualified boolean localStorage key with no user component — is false in this working tree. offline-persistence-preference.ts stores a JSON *array of consenting user ids* (setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(userId, enabled) at :134-157 adds/removes only that one id; :146 JSON.stringify(next)), and getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(userId) at :103-110 returns consentingIds().includes(userId), defaulting to false for an absent identity. parseConsent at :59-72 deliberately reads a legacy bare "true" as nobody-consented, so the exact cross-account carryover described cannot occur even after a migration. Every enforcement call site passes the identity: collab-document-provider.tsx:219-224 (useOfflinePersistenceEnabled(personId)), use-durable-document.ts:121/131, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:185-187 (isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(userId) && isOfflineWritePermitted(userId)), and settings/page.tsx:38-39/148 — so user B's Settings switch reads off, not "already-on". The only device-wide read, hasOfflinePersistenceConsent() at collab-document-provider.tsx:238-242, is used solely while identityPending; when it is true, identified is false (:242), ready is false (:286), and the component returns null (:362-364) instead of mounting a durable client, so no content is written to disk on another account's consent. The described vector is not reachable as stated.
